title: Wild-type sign agreement gave no clear mutant prediction gain in 722 selected worm pairs
abstract: We tested whether wild-type pooled response sign agreement helps predict unc-31 agreement after wiring, sampling and cell controls. We linked the Randi response atlas to two adult Witvliet maps by cell name. The primary sample had 722 directed pairs and 33 stimulated identities. Five folds held out source families from both training roles. Adding wild-type agreement changed equal-source mean squared error from 0.07198736 to 0.07199759. The reduction was -0.00001024, with a nominal conditional 95 percent shared-cell interval from -0.00044558 to 0.00040091. All six sensitivity intervals included zero. Sparse mutant lists, pooled observations without animal labels, separate anatomy animals and fixed-fit intervals leave cross-condition transfer unresolved. This is not a biological reliability or equivalence claim. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: WT agreement gave no clear added mutant prediction gain. Bars show conditional shared-cell bootstrap intervals. All intervals include zero.
